business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010 de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y del financiamiento del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 7/2021); Royal Decree 304/2014 establishing the UBO central register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP status screening under Ley 10/2010, OFAC SDN list, UN consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and domestic AEAT tax authority cross-checks

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (e-Registro Mercantil online portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official Spanish language; names must use Latin alphabet; foreign names require Spanish translation or adaptation per Registro Mercantil rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal within one month to the Registro Mercantil Central; upon rejection, pursue judicial review before the Audiencia Provincial

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for SL entities; virtual offices accepted for administrative and tax compliance purposes provided a real registered address exists for regulatory filings
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for data center colocation leasing industry; unannounced inspections primarily triggered by AML/CFT red flags or tax authority requests

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for SL formation plus prevailing market benchmark for multinational due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and registry filing fees
Notarization and apostille services for foreign documents
UBO and PEP screening and compliance setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Law (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-30, 32, 62, 78-81, 210-245, and 252-253; Law 14/2013 and Law 18/2022 concerning electronic formation and minimum capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office, coordinated with the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) containing the articles of association, followed by registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. A mandatory escrow account does not exist. For cash contributions, a bank certificate may be submitted; alternatively, the founders may dispense with the certificate and assume joint liability for the reality of the contributions under Article 62.2. If capital is below EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until capital plus reserve reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholder liability applies on liquidation up to the difference.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Company Name], S.L., duly constituted on [date], resolves: (1) to acknowledge and approve the subscription and full payment of the share capital of EUR [amount] by the founding shareholder(s), as recorded in the incorporation deed; (2) to adopt [full address] as the Company’s registered office; (3) to appoint [name] as sole director, or [names] as directors, with the powers stated in the articles and applicable law; (4) to authorize the appointed officer(s) to obtain the NIF, register the Company with tax and social-security authorities, open bank accounts, and complete all incorporation filings; and (5) to approve the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its electronic name-certification service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identify the founding applicant, pay the applicable certificate charge, and obtain the negative name certificate. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for reservation purposes. Use the exact certified name in all subsequent instruments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or challenge the refusal through the Central Commercial Registry’s administrative review channels. Correct discrepancies before requesting the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (Notario) and the competent Provincial Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, ownership structure, corporate purpose, registered office, capital allocation, management model, and beneficial-owner declaration. Obtain Spanish foreigner identification numbers (NIE) for non-resident founders, directors, and beneficial owners where required. Foreign corporate documents must be apostilled or legalized, translated into Spanish by a sworn translator, and supported by evidence of signing authority.
required_dossiers: Founders’ passports or national identity documents
Foreign corporate constitutional documents and powers of attorney
Capital contribution evidence or statutory founders’ declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the notary’s compliance requests, correct legalization or translation defects, and replace defective powers of attorney before execution. Obtain updated registry extracts for foreign corporate shareholders if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed and obtain provisional tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public and State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary. The deed must identify the founders, contributions, shares, articles, management body, registered office, and beneficial owner. Apply to the AEAT for the provisional tax identification number (NIF) using Form 036, normally through the notary or an authorized representative.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution certificate or founders’ declaration
Public deed draft approved by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected Form 036 filings or incomplete identity records and resubmit through the AEAT electronic system or authorized representative. Rectify the deed by notarial instrument if the notary identifies a substantive defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authorized electronic or paper copy of the public deed, provisional NIF documentation, beneficial-owner information, and required registry forms. Pay the applicable registry and publication charges. The registry examiner verifies statutory compliance, corporate name, capital, management structure, registered office, and corporate purpose before issuing registration.
required_dossiers: Authorized copy of the public deed
Foreign-document legalization and translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect notice, cure each defect within the applicable validity period, refile the corrected instrument, and request a new examination. A formal appeal may be filed with the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith or the competent court, subject to statutory deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, accounting, and employment registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and the relevant regional employment authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Replace the provisional NIF with the definitive NIF using Form 036 after Commercial Registry registration. Register the applicable economic activities and tax obligations. Legalize accounting books electronically with the Commercial Registry and file the annual accounts in accordance with Spanish accounting law. If personnel are hired, obtain an employer contribution account and register employees before work begins.
required_dossiers: Registered deed and Commercial Registry certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct activity codes, tax obligations, or social-security records through amended filings. Respond to AEAT or Social Security information requests with documentary evidence and maintain proof of electronic submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt governance controls and operational authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company’s governing body, relevant autonomous-community industrial authority, and the municipality where the data center operates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve the registered office, officers, bank mandates, accounting policy, related-party controls, data-security framework, and delegated signing authorities. Before construction or operation, obtain municipal planning, building, activity, and opening authorizations and register applicable electrical, high-voltage, backup-generation, pressure-equipment, and fire-protection installations with the competent autonomous-community authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure technical or documentary observations issued by the municipality or autonomous community, request inspection reattendance where permitted, and appeal refusals under the applicable regional administrative procedure. Do not commence regulated physical operations before required authorizations are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The industrial authority of the autonomous community in which the facility is located, together with the relevant municipal authority. There is no single nationwide data-center operating-license board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No universal national data-center operating permit. The facility may require a municipal activity or environmental authorization, building and opening authorization, and autonomous-community registration or commissioning certificates for electrical, high-voltage, generator, pressure, and fire-protection installations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional: generally no automatic full EIA solely because the activity is data-center colocation; a simplified or ordinary EIA may apply if the project falls within statutory annexes, exceeds applicable capacity thresholds, involves listed locations, or forms part of a qualifying infrastructure project. Municipal environmental licensing may still be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable discharge authorization and limits under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2001 and basin-authority requirements; manage batteries, oils, refrigerants, electronic equipment, and other wastes under Law 7/2022 and implementing rules; control generator and other air emissions under Law 34/2007 and regional permits; obtain permits for hazardous waste and maintain traceability, inspections, and authorized-operator records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal or regional fire-safety approval based on the Technical Building Code, including DB-SI, and, where applicable, the Regulation on Fire Safety in Industrial Establishments under Royal Decree 2267/2004. Commission fire detection, suppression, emergency power, evacuation, and structural systems through qualified technicians. Complete electrical and structural-load inspections, occupational risk assessment, emergency planning, worker training, and prevention-service arrangements under Law 31/1995 and applicable implementing regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Spain's State Agency for Tax Administration, through the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. Customs and indirect-tax formalities are administered through the AEAT's customs and excise systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT. The incorporation process normally uses a provisional NIF requested with Form 036, the deed of incorporation, the certification of the company name, and identification and authority documents for the legal representative. After registration with the Commercial Registry, the company files Form 036 to obtain or confirm the definitive NIF and update its registered data, activities, tax addresses, shareholders, directors, and beneficial ownership information where required. A non-established foreign entity carrying out taxable transactions in Spain must generally obtain a Spanish NIF by filing Form 036 with the AEAT and providing its constitutional documents, certificate of existence or registry extract, tax-residence evidence where relevant, Spanish tax representative or authorized agent details when required, and identification documents for its representatives. Documents issued outside Spain may require apostille or legalization and a sworn Spanish translation. A non-established business making intra-Community supplies or acquisitions must additionally register in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain an ES-prefixed VAT identification number. An EORI number is required for customs operations. VAT registration is generally integrated into the Form 036 registration process; there is no general Spanish turnover threshold below which a person carrying on taxable Spanish economic activity is automatically outside VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person and has no general United States-style check-the-box election or general pass-through election. Available statutory regimes may include the tax-consolidation regime for qualifying Spanish tax groups, the special regime for entities holding foreign securities (ETVE) where statutory participation and substance requirements are met, and other sector-specific regimes. These regimes require formal eligibility and, in relevant cases, an election or prior notification. Spanish and EU anti-hybrid-mismatch rules deny or neutralize deductions, exemptions, or other benefits for specified hybrid instruments, entities, permanent establishments, and imported mismatch arrangements; they do not provide a general elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), governed principally by Law 37/1992 and related regulations. Spain also applies customs duties and other indirect taxes under EU and Spanish legislation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold applies in mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands for commencement of taxable business activity. A person carrying on an economic activity must generally register for VAT purposes before commencing the activity or making relevant taxable transactions. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of Spanish VAT and have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spanish VAT taxpayers must issue invoices meeting Royal Decree 1619/2012 requirements and preserve them electronically or otherwise in an auditable form. The Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers in the monthly VAT refund regime, large enterprises exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, and VAT groups, to submit invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT generally within four business days, subject to statutory adjustments. Spain has legislated a phased private-sector electronic-invoicing framework for business-to-business transactions under Law 18/2022, with implementation dependent on the applicable implementing regulation and taxpayer size. This framework is distinct from universal real-time VAT clearance. The AEAT's VERI*FACTU and related certified billing-system requirements introduce anti-tampering, traceability, QR, and electronic-record obligations under the applicable implementation timetable; they do not currently create a universal pre-clearance requirement for every invoice. Public-sector electronic invoicing is mandatory for covered suppliers through FACe or the relevant public-administration platform. Data-center colocation invoices are generally subject to 21% Spanish VAT when the place-of-supply rules locate the service in Spain. B2B services supplied to a business customer established outside Spain may instead be outside Spanish VAT under the general customer-location rule, subject to exceptions and evidence requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify as VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT under the export provisions of Law 37/1992, provided the supplier or an authorized intermediary can substantiate both the export transaction and the actual exit of the goods from the EU customs territory. The treatment is technically an exemption with right of deduction rather than a domestic 0% rate. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and reporting and documentary requirements are satisfied. Services are not automatically zero-rated because they are described as exports. A B2B service supplied to a customer established outside Spain is generally outside Spanish VAT under the general place-of-supply rule, subject to special rules for immovable-property, admission, transport, telecommunications, electronically supplied, and other specified services. For data-center colocation, the analysis must distinguish bare rack or hosting services from services sufficiently connected with immovable property; the contractual facts, customer status, establishment receiving the service, and physical use of the facility are material. Evidence should include customer tax status, contractual scope, service-location analysis, customer establishment, and any required reverse-charge statement. A VAT refund for a non-established business is available only under the applicable EU or non-EU refund procedure and subject to reciprocity, representation, filing, invoice, and deadline requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration filed through the Spanish or EU customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN), export accompanying document, and export-acceptance data
Customs office of exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods physically exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, consignee, description, value, Incoterms, and transaction terms
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent evidence
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery records, and transport or freight-forwarder evidence linking the goods to the export declaration
Proof of payment or other commercial settlement evidence where relevant to establish the transaction's reality
Import customs documentation or destination-country receipt evidence where available
Valid customer VAT identification and intra-Community transport evidence for exempt intra-Community supplies, where applicable
Bank or inward-remittance evidence may support commercial substantiation but is not, by itself, a legal substitute for customs proof of export and is not a universal Spanish VAT-export requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for VAT export exemption. Spanish foreign-exchange rules generally permit cross-border payments without a universal export-proceeds repatriation deadline, although anti-money-laundering, customs, accounting, banking, and statistical-reporting obligations may apply. If export exemption or an input-VAT refund is claimed without valid proof of transport or exit, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, and may deny or claw back related input-VAT deductions or refunds. Administrative penalties under General Tax Law 58/2003 are fact-dependent and may include proportional penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly obtained or unpaid tax, with higher percentages for aggravating circumstances, concealment, repeated non-compliance, or fraudulent conduct. Separate penalties may apply for incorrect invoices, deficient records, failure to report intra-Community transactions, or customs violations. Customs non-compliance may result in recovery of duties and import VAT, interest, and national or EU customs sanctions. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding the applicable criminal threshold may constitute a tax offense under the Spanish Criminal Code, potentially involving fines and imprisonment. The taxpayer must retain invoices, contracts, transport records, customs data, electronic exit evidence, and accounting records for the statutory audit and limitation periods, generally four years for Spanish tax assessment purposes, subject to suspension, interruption, or longer retention requirements under other laws.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), together with the Directorate-General of the Treasury and Financial Policy of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise. Spain applies the European Union framework for capital movements, payments, payment services, anti-money laundering, and prudential supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account purposes. Spain generally has no exchange-control approval requirement for foreign investment, shareholder funding, intercompany loans, dividend payments, interest, royalties, service fees, or liquidation proceeds. Cross-border payments remain subject to bank-level AML, sanctions, tax, beneficial-ownership, and source-of-funds controls. Profit remittances require distributable accounting profits, approval of the competent corporate body, compliance with legal-reserve and balance-sheet requirements, withholding-tax analysis, and documentation supporting the underlying transaction. Non-resident investment and foreign financing may trigger statistical, investment, or tax reporting obligations depending on transaction type, counterparty, amount, and applicable reporting regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted commercially through an authorized bank. The company must maintain invoices, contracts, transport or delivery evidence, customs records where applicable, and payment records. Banks may request transaction-purpose, beneficiary, origin-of-funds, and trade documentation. Statistical, tax, customs, foreign-investment, balance-of-payments, and AML reporting may apply, particularly for material or unusual cross-border transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with SEPA, SWIFT, collection, payroll, and FX capabilities
Operational Account with SEPA, SWIFT, treasury, and foreign-currency capabilities
Operational Account with SEPA, domestic payment, trade-finance, and FX capabilities
Operational Account with SEPA, SWIFT, trade-finance, and foreign-currency capabilities
Operational Account with SEPA, SWIFT, treasury, and corporate-payment capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment execution, collections, SEPA access, and selected foreign-currency services, but not equivalent to a Spanish bank account. An offshore digital EMI cannot automatically provide regulated services in Spain unless it is authorized under the applicable EEA passporting framework or operates through an appropriately authorized local structure. The EMI must hold the required payment or electronic-money authorization, safeguard customer funds, comply with AML and sanctions rules, and observe PSD2, applicable strong customer authentication, safeguarding, complaints, outsourcing, and data-protection requirements. EMIs generally cannot accept repayable deposits or provide ordinary bank credit. Availability of Spanish IBANs, SWIFT connectivity, local tax-payment functions, cash services, direct debit sponsorship, and account stability depends on the provider. A Spanish SL should retain a regulated Spanish or EEA bank account for statutory payments, payroll, tax, reserve liquidity, and contingency purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by directors is not generally mandated by Spanish law for ordinary corporate-bank onboarding. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified documentation, and beneficial-owner verification. Individual bank policy may nevertheless require a branch meeting, live video interview, notarized powers of attorney, wet-ink signatures, or in-person verification where directors, shareholders, jurisdictions, business activity, payment corridors, or ownership chains present elevated risk. Foreign corporate documents commonly require apostille or legalization, sworn Spanish translation where required, current registry extracts, and evidence of authority. The bank must identify the company, directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, business purpose, expected activity, source of funds, and expected counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-layered ownership structure, nominee shareholders, trusts, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish Commercial Registry extract; constitutional documents; complete ownership chart to natural persons; shareholder registers; identity and address evidence for all relevant owners; beneficial-owner declaration; trust or nominee documentation where applicable; board resolution appointing signatories; and legal opinion or corporate secretarial certification explaining the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder funding, intercompany loans, or capital injections without a clear source and economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; bank statements evidencing source of funds; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; tax-residence certificates; group organizational chart; transfer-pricing or arm's-length support where relevant; remittance advice; and written explanation of the funding purpose and expected use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data-center colocation and bare-metal hosting activity viewed as cyber-risk, virtual-asset exposure, prohibited-content risk, or high-risk technology activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service catalogue; customer acceptance and prohibited-use policy; master service agreements; acceptable-use and sanctions clauses; customer due-diligence procedures; incident-response and cybersecurity policies; evidence that the company does not operate a virtual-asset exchange or custody business; data-center lease or colocation agreement; insurance evidence; and sample invoices showing ordinary hosting and rack-space services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment flows inconsistent with the stated business, including unexplained high-value cross-border wires, rapid pass-through transactions, or payments involving unrelated third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume and currency matrix; customer and supplier concentration schedule; representative contracts and invoices; expected countries and counterparties; payment approval matrix; reconciliation procedures; treasury policy; and explanation of intercompany, customer-refund, deposit, and pass-through flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, high-risk-country, or correspondent-bank exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening and escalation policy; PEP declarations; identity documents; source-of-wealth evidence where required; customer and supplier screening records; country-risk assessment; enhanced due-diligence report; contractual sanctions representations; and documented approval by the compliance officer for higher-risk relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing Spanish tax, corporate, or operational substance evidence, particularly where the company is newly incorporated or directors and shareholders are non-resident.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax identification number; Commercial Registry documents; registered office evidence; director and signatory appointments; lease, colocation, or service agreements; employee or contractor evidence where applicable; Spanish tax registrations; business plan; projected customer base; accounting engagement letter; and evidence of the operational relationship with the Spanish data-center facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, third-party payment accounts, unlicensed payment intermediaries, or digital wallets for company receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy prohibiting personal and unauthorized third-party accounts; approved bank and EMI list; payment-control matrix; account ownership confirmations; reconciliation controls; onboarding records for payment providers; and evidence that customer funds are not held or commingled contrary to applicable payment-services rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, share-premium funding, and intercompany loans from the documented funding entity directly to the Spanish SL's account at a regulated bank or appropriately authorized EEA payment institution. Use a payment narrative identifying the legal basis, such as share capital subscription, shareholder contribution, share premium, or intercompany loan. Spain does not generally use a universal statutory FX purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires; the bank may instead require its own payment-purpose classification and supporting documents. Before remittance, prepare the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds documentation, tax analysis, and any applicable foreign-investment or statistical filings. Reconcile the incoming payment to the accounting ledger and preserve SWIFT or SEPA confirmation, bank statements, and supporting corporate documents. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group companies, unlicensed intermediaries, or opaque payment wallets.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro supplier payments within the SEPA area and SEPA Direct Debit for authorized recurring collections where the company is the payer or creditor under the relevant mandate framework. Use SWIFT cross-border credit transfers for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions; legacy MT103 terminology may still be used operationally, although banks are migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages. Provide accurate originator, beneficiary, invoice, purpose, and intermediary-bank information. For imports or material equipment purchases, use documentary collections or a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under UCP 600, with documentary examination and sanctions screening. For data-center equipment, bandwidth, hosting, cloud, insurance, maintenance, and professional services, maintain contracts, purchase orders, invoices, delivery or service evidence, VAT treatment, withholding-tax analysis, and three-way payment-to-accounting reconciliation. Apply dual authorization, beneficiary-change callback controls, payment limits, sanctions screening, and segregation of preparation and approval functions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts with an authorized bank or eligible regulated investment firm, documented under the provider's master agreement and supported by a genuine forecast or committed exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where local-currency delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to counterparty eligibility, product suitability, collateral, reporting, and applicable derivatives rules. NDFs are generally less relevant for ordinary EUR/USD or EUR/GBP exposures where deliverable forwards are available.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps for recurring funding, debt-service, or long-dated currency mismatches, subject to counterparty credit approval, valuation, collateral, accounting, and EMIR-related requirements where applicable.
FX options or collars may be used for asymmetric exposures, subject to suitability, premium, valuation, accounting, and derivatives-governance controls.

Hedging must be linked to identifiable commercial, financing, or balance-sheet exposures; speculative dealing should be prohibited by treasury policy. Maintain board-approved limits, counterparty limits, confirmations, independent valuation, hedge-accounting documentation where elected, collateral procedures, and periodic effectiveness testing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) in the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office in Spain
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval must occur within six months after fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end: deposit by July 31 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry fine up to EUR 6,000; annual accounts are not admitted for deposit; once the register is closed, no certificate of good standing can be obtained; continued default can lead to cancellation of the register entry after 6 years and opening of a judicial insolvency procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades – Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 July and 25 July following a December 31 year-end (first 25 days of July); for a company with a non-calendar year-end, within 25 days after six months from the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 5% plus 1% per month for late filing; late-payment interest; penalties of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 depending on omissions; no strike-off, but tax enforcement is independent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legalization of Accounting Books (Legalización anual de libros contables)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (through its telematic or physical presentation system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end: before April 30 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounting books lose evidential force; company may be barred from filing subsequent annual accounts; administrative fine of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 under commercial regulation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Return on Third-Party Transactions (Declaración informativa – Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 29 February of the following calendar year when total annual transactions with any single counterparty exceed EUR 3,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 150 per incorrectly or omitted record, minimum EUR 1,000 and maximum EUR 6,000 for the total information return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Summary Return (Resumen anual de retenciones – Modelo 190)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 and 31 January of the following calendar year, summarizing withheld IRPF on salaries and professional fees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 150 per data item with a minimum of EUR 300; if the return is filed after a formal demand, additional penalty of 1% per month up to 20% of the tax withheld.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Spanish Law/Corporate Enterprises Act, an audit is required when a company meets at least two of the following criteria for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average headcount above 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP under the Plan General Contable (PGC); consolidated accounts in Spain must be prepared under IFRS as adopted by the EU. Individual company accounts of an SL are also in PGC with no IFRS option.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish law does not require an annual UBO filing for an SL when no ownership changes occur; all transfers of quota shares must be entered in the Libro Registro de Socios and registered at the Registro Mercantil, with an updated beneficial-ownership declaration (titularidad real) filed within one month of any change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro Registro de Administradores (Register of Directors)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Book)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general CIT rate (Ley 27/2014, Art. 29.1; 2024-2025 fiscal years)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs (including data centre colocation businesses) on the first €300,000 of taxable base in the first two profitable tax periods (cumulative annual cap €1M? Actually per tax period cap of €300,000? The cap applies to per period €300k? I recall cap of €300,000 taxable base per given period); 25%/(42% incremental) R&D tax deduction (Art. 35 LIS); 10% capitalisation reserve deduction on retained profits up to 10%(?)...
corporate_income_tax_regime.loss_carryforward_policy_notes: Indefinite carryforward under Art. 26 LIS; annual offset capped at 70% of positive taxable base for turnovers < €1M (floor €1M), 60% for €1M-€20M, 50% for >€20M.
